title: 数字和颜色
intro: Counting to a thousand, ages, prices, dates and colours. Chinese numbers are perfectly regular: 十一 = 10+1, 二十 = 2×10, 一百零二 = 102. Watch 两 vs 二, 几 vs 多少, and the 一 sandhi in 一百 yì bǎi.

items.note: 四 sì sounds close to 死 sǐ (death), so 4 is an unlucky number; many buildings skip the 4th floor.

ex.p: wǒ sì suì
wǒ jiā yǒu sì gè rén
ex.en: There are four people in my family.

ex.p: wǒ yǒu wǔ gè píng guǒ
yī zhī shǒu yǒu wǔ gēn shǒu zhǐ

items.note: 6 is lucky: 六六大顺 'everything goes smoothly'.

ex.p: wǒ liù suì le
liù gè xiǎo péng you zài wánr
yé ye qī shí suì
yī gè xīng qī yǒu qī tiān

items.note: 8 bā rhymes with 发 fā (get rich): the luckiest number.

ex.p: bā diǎn le qǐ chuáng ba
xiǎo gǒu bā suì le

items.note: 九 jiǔ sounds like 久 jiǔ (long-lasting).

ex.p: wǒ jiǔ diǎn shuì jiào
ex.en: I go to bed at nine.

ex.p: wǒ yǒu jiǔ kuài qián

items.note: Fills a gap in a number: 一百零二 = 102. Written 〇 in years: 二〇二六年.

ex.p: èr líng èr liù nián
yī bǎi líng yī zhī xiǎo gǒu

items.note: 一百 is yì bǎi (sandhi).

ex.p: wǒ yǒu yī bǎi kuài qián
wǒ kǎo le yī bǎi fēn
ex.en: I got a hundred points on the test!

items.note: Chinese counts in 万 (ten thousand) next: 一万 = 10,000.

ex.p: yī qiān kuài qián tài duō le
ex.en: A thousand yuan is too much.

ex.p: tiān shàng yǒu jǐ qiān kē xīng xing
ex.en: There are thousands of stars in the sky.

items.note: Counting things: 两个人, not 二个人. Counting, digits and ordinals use 二: 一二三, 十二, 第二.

ex.p: wǒ yào liǎng gè píng guǒ
wǒ yǒu liǎng zhī xiǎo gǒu

items.note: 几 + measure word asks about a number you expect to be under ten.

ex.p: nǐ jǐ suì
ex.en: How old are you? (to a child)

ex.p: nǐ yǒu jǐ gè dì di
ex.en: How many younger brothers do you have?

items.note: 多少 can skip the measure word: 多少人？

ex.p: duō shao qián
nǐ jiā yǒu duō shao běn shū
ex.en: How many books do you have at home?

items.note: No 是 needed: 我五岁.

ex.p: nǐ jǐ suì le
wǒ mèi mei sān suì

items.note: In speech prices use 块 (written: 元 yuán).

ex.p: zhè ge píng guǒ liǎng kuài qián
gěi nǐ yī kuài táng

items.note: As a noun it's shù: 数学 math, 数字 number. 数数 = shǔ shù, 'count numbers'.

ex.p: wǒ huì shǔ shù
nǐ shǔ yī shǔ yǒu jǐ gè

items.note: Before a verb it means 'more': 多吃 eat more.

ex.p: zhè lǐ rén hěn duō
ex.en: There are lots of people here.

ex.p: duō chī shuǐ guǒ

items.note: Before a verb: 'less'. 少 shào (young) is another reading: 少年.

ex.p: táng yào shǎo chī
gōng yuán lǐ rén hěn shǎo
ex.en: There are few people in the park.

ex.p: wǒ shì dì yī
dì èr gè shì wǒ de

items.note: Dates go big to small: 2026年11月22号.

ex.p: jīn tiān jǐ hào
wǒ de shēng rì shì wǔ yuè bā hào
yī gòng duō shao qián
wǒ men yī gòng yǒu wǔ gè rén
ex.en: There are five of us in total.

items.note: Red = luck and celebration (red envelopes, weddings). 色 is sè; in casual northern speech also shǎi.

ex.p: wǒ xǐ huan hóng sè
hóng sè de píng guǒ hěn hǎo chī

items.note: Careful: 黄色 can also mean 'pornographic' (黄色电影).

ex.p: xiāng jiāo shì huáng sè de

ex.zh: 我有一只黄色的小鸭子。
ex.p: wǒ yǒu yī zhī huáng sè de xiǎo yā zi
ex.en: I have a little yellow duck.

ex.p: tiān shì lán sè de
gē ge xǐ huan lán sè

items.note: Never give a man a green hat (绿帽子): it means his wife is cheating.

ex.p: xiǎo cǎo shì lǜ sè de
wǒ de shū bāo shì lǜ sè de

items.note: White is the traditional colour of mourning.

ex.p: xiǎo bái tù shì bái sè de
wǒ yǒu yī jiàn bái sè de yī fu
xiǎo māo shì hēi sè de
bà ba de chē shì hēi sè de
nǐ xǐ huan shén me yán sè
zhè shì shén me yán sè

items.note: 喜欢 + verb: 喜欢吃, 喜欢玩儿.

ex.p: wǒ xǐ huan xiǎo gǒu
nǐ xǐ huan chī shén me
ex.en: What do you like to eat?

四.h: A box with two legs inside. The oldest form was simply four lines.

五.h: Lines crossing between heaven and earth.

六.h: A little hut: roof 亠 over 八.

七.h: A cross with its tail cut and bent.

八.h: Two strokes parting: eight, and 'to divide'.

九.h: A bent arm reaching out: the biggest digit.

零.h: Rain 雨 + 令 for the sound: leftover drops → zero.

百.h: 一 + 白 bái for the sound.

两.h: A yoke for two animals: a pair.

几.h: A small table 几; borrowed for 'how many'.

多.h: Evening 夕 on evening 夕: many.

少.h: 小 small with a bit more cut away: few.

岁.h: A mountain 山 of evenings 夕: your years.

块.h: Earth 土 + 夬 for the sound: a lump.

数.h: Tapping 攵 grains of rice 米 one by one.

第.h: Bamboo slips ⺮ in order like brothers 弟.

号.h: A mouth 口 calling out a number.

红.h: Silk 纟 + 工 for the sound: red-dyed silk.

黄.h: The colour of the loess soil of the Yellow River.

蓝.h: Indigo plant 艹 + 监 for the sound.

绿.h: Silk 纟 + 录 for the sound.

白.h: A ray of sunlight: white, bright.

黑.h: A sooty chimney over fire 灬: black.

喜.h: A drum 壴 and a singing mouth 口: joy. 囍 double joy is the wedding symbol.

欢.h: Hand 又 + 欠 (open mouth): happy cheering.

texts.title: 一二三，爬上山

lines.p: yī èr sān pá shàng shān
lines.en: One, two, three, climb up the hill;

lines.p: sì wǔ liù fān gēn tou
lines.en: four, five, six, turn a somersault;

lines.p: qī bā jiǔ pāi pí qiú
lines.en: seven, eight, nine, bounce the ball;

notes: Counting 一二三 keeps 一 as yī (no sandhi in counting).
翻跟头 fān gēn tou: to do a somersault. 拍皮球: to bounce a rubber ball.

texts.title: 山村咏怀（一去二三里）
texts.src: 邵雍 Shào Yōng (1011–1077), Northern Song · public domain

lines.en: Off we go, two or three li,
a smoky village of four or five homes.
lines.mod: 路边的小村子里有四五户人家，冒着炊烟。

lines.en: eight, nine, ten sprigs of flowers.

notes: Often the first poem a Chinese child learns: the numbers 一 to 十 appear in order.
里 lǐ: a traditional distance, about 500 m. 烟 here is cooking smoke rising from chimneys. 亭台: pavilions and terraces.
一去 is yí qù: 一 before a 4th tone.

qs.q: Write the first line from memory.

texts.title: 数数歌（上山打老虎）

lines.en: up the hill to hunt a tiger.

notes: The most famous Chinese counting rhyme.
没打到: didn't manage to hit/catch. 数来又数去: counted over and over.

texts.title: 颜色歌

lines.p: wǒ xǐ huan shén me yán sè

notes: Doubling an adjective (红红的) makes it vivid and childlike.
Colours drop 色 before 的 in this pattern: 红红的, not 红色红色的.

exercises.why: Before a measure word, 2 is 两: 两个.
几 for small numbers you expect to be under 10, like a child's age. 多少 for any number.
You expect a big number, so 多少.

exercises.p: wǒ yǒu liǎng gè mèi mei

exercises.why: 色 comes last in colour words.
Tens first: 十五 = 10 + 5. 五十 = 5 × 10 = 50.
A missing tens digit becomes 零. Careful: 一百二 means 120.

scenario.title: 小卖部买东西
scenario.setting: You're six and buying snacks at the little corner shop on your own for the first time.

a.p: xiǎo péng you nǐ yào mǎi shén me
a.en: What would you like to buy, little one?

opts.p: wǒ yào liǎng gè píng guǒ
wǒ yào èr gè píng guǒ
opts.fb: Before 个, use 两: 两个苹果.
Understood, but 我要… is the polite full form.
She just told you: 五块.

d.npc: 谢谢！你要红色的袋子还是蓝色的？
d.p: xiè xie nǐ yào hóng sè de dài zi hái shi lán sè de
d.en: Thanks! Do you want a red bag or a blue one?

opts.fb: Colour + 的 stands in for the noun: 红色的 = the red one.

e.p: gěi nǐ ná hǎo zài jiàn
e.en: Here you go. Hold on to it, bye!
